As a SUPV IT SPECIALIST (PLCYPLN), GS-2210-13, you will perform the following duties: 1. Manages, plans, organizes, controls, and directs the communications activities for the Wing and Base to ensure mission accomplishment and optimum use of resources.

Sets policy, directs and monitors support and related programs including planning and programming, funds distribution and management, economic analysis assistance, budget administration, material management, and related activities.

Establishes, advises, and consults on production and quality requirements, mission objectives, equipment requirements and other logistics needs, to ensure requirements satisfy the respective mission sets and obligations.

Plans and institutes communications fiscal policies to implement federal law, higher level directives, and to provide optimum support to subordinate organizations.

Maintains required information assurance certification IAW DoD 8570.01-M, Federal Information Security Management Act of 2002, Clinger Cohen Act of 1996, in order to ensure the rigorous application of information security and information assurance policies, principles, and practices in the delivery of all information technology services.

Responsible for unit level oversight of programs used to monitor and eliminate fraud, waste, abuse and mismanagement. Supports audit programs within the Communications unit. Serves as a functional area technical expert to the Financial Management Board (FMB).

Responsible for the development, management, and execution of financial management plans as they relate to communications systems. Analyzes, evaluates, validates, and recommends approval and disapproval of requested or proposed system requirements and develops documentation used in the processing and validation of such requirements. 2.

Coordinates communications activities and projects with other concerned agencies and organizations. Determines goals and objectives for the organization.

Exercises supervisory responsibility and authority including granting leave, appraising performance, establishing performance standards, recommending promotions, and initiating disciplinary actions as needed. Gives advice, counsel, and instructions to supervisors and subordinate incumbents on both general policy and administrative matters.

Provides guidance and direction to unit members through a variety of methods in support of several functions, to include maintenance, logistics plans, supply, multimedia, quality control, production control, ground radio, telecommunications, software applications, technical services, networks, computer programs, and computer systems operations.

Consults with subordinate supervisorsand training specialists on training needs. Develops strategies for the hiring, training, and professional development of Wing communications personnel. Makes decisions on work problems presented by subordinate supervisors.

Evaluates subordinate supervisors and reviews evaluations made by subordinate supervisors on other incumbents. Recommends selections for subordinate positions. Hears and resolves grievances and serious incumbent complaints not resolved at a lower level.

Reviews serious disciplinary cases and disciplinary problems involving subordinates incumbents and determines required action. Supports equal employment opportunity and labor-management relations programs. Ensures efficient position management is practiced and that position descriptions of subordinates are accurate. 3.

Coordinates with support organizations to assure an integrated approach to solution of problems. Assesses the impact of changes in the local area network and coordinates with operations to ensure these changes do not exceed maintenance or unit capabilities.

Ensures unit Quality Assurance and Standardization and Evaluation programs are effectively managed. Develops new procedures to solve unprecedented technical problems. 4. Ensures formulation of comprehensive training plans for each function and specialty within the C4 and logistics activity.

Develops CONUS and overseas deployment plans to meet unit's mission goals, inspection schedules, and deployment requirements. Identifies the need for facility and equipment modernization, improvements and replacements. Coordinates planning activities and resources with other units and higher headquarters.

Manages the development of unit training goals and long range training plans. Assures that training sustains work force qualifications and capabilities. Oversees the unit mobility program. Performs other duties as assigned. *The above duty description does not contain all details of the official position description.

A copy of the entire position description can be found on FASCLASS by searching the position description PD#: (D2170P01). https://acpol2.army.mil/fasclass/search_fs/search_fasclass.asp
GENERAL EXPERIENCE: For all positions individuals must have IT-related experience demonstrating each of the four competencies listed below. The employing agency is responsible for identifying the specific level of proficiency required for each competency at each grade level based on the requirements of the position being filled.

Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail.

Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services.

Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately.

Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations.

Including experience, education, and/or training that has provided a basic knowledge of data processing functions and general management principles that enabled the applicant to understand the stages required to automate a work process.

Experience may have been gained in work such as computer operator or assistant, computer sales representative, program analyst, or other positions that required the use or adaptation of computer programs and systems.

SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: 1-year equivalent to at least next lower grade level experience that has equipped the applicant with the particular competencies/knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position and is typically in or related to the work of the position to be filled.

Such experience is typically gained in the IT field or through the performance of work where the primary concern is IT.

The Supervisory Information Technology Specialist serves as the Facilities and Physical Security Branch (FPSB) Chief within the Business Administration System and Support Division (BASSD).

The incumbent focuses on managing FPSB staff and providing leadership through clear communication, employee development, performance management, conflict resolution, guidance, and recognition of contributions to help employees grow and achieve team objectives.

The position reports to the Business Administration System and Support Division (BASSD) Chief and manages federal and contractual resources to support initiatives across the administrative business portfolio. The incumbent works in a customer-focused environment where high-quality deliverables must be completed on time.

Duties include, but are not limited to: Providing solutions architecture and broad technology support Providing knowledge and direction to staff in the current technical environment, including Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL/MariaDB, Pentaho, .NET, Java, PHP, ColdFusion, JavaScript, and other technologies.

Establishing and ensuring consistent system development methodologies, templates, guidelines, checklists, and other artifacts to support repeatable processes. Supervising multiple software development teams and ensuring appropriate resource staffing levels.

Implementing appropriate change control processes across development teams and ensuring integration across teams throughout the Judiciary. Assisting in defining the strategic direction for standardizing common technologies and toolsets. Developing and implementing coding security procedures.

Working with the Chief Technology Officer and other senior management to implement solutions that align with the CIO strategic plans, enterprise architecture standards, and security best practices.

Participating in associated change control boards by reviewing change requests and evaluating the completeness of request documentation and potential risk impacts to the Judiciary.
Applicants must have demonstrated experience as listed below. This requirement is according to the AO Classification, Compensation, and Recruitment Systems which include interpretive guidance and reference to the OPM Operating Manual for Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions.

Specialized Experience: Applicants must have at least one full year (52 weeks) of specialized experience which is in or directly related to the line of work of this position.

Specialized experience is demonstrated experience must demonstrate ALL areas defined below: Leading and managing information technology teams responsible for the development, implementation, and support of enterprise business systems and solutions.

Supporting enterprise business systems and solutions that support administrative functions such as human resources, finance, facilities, or other organizational operations.

Developing, implementing, or overseeing enterprise technology solutions using system development methodologies, system architecture, data management practices, and related technologies.

As a IT Specialist (Applications Software), you will perform the following duties: Serve as a Geospatial Data Engineer applying mastery level expertise to initiate and lead application software development projects through development, coding, testing, evaluating, operational implementation and support of software.

Utilize applications including Python, Integrated Development Environments, XML and geospatial applications such as QGIS to support cloud-based computing for National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) hydrographic data acquisition platforms and Office of Coast Survey (OCS).

Lead and ensure continuous and efficient operation of NOAA hydrographic platforms and Coast Survey office by providing timely support of operational software, including in-house and third-party software, and their integration. Lead the analysis of existing software and systems to identify opportunities for improvement, automation, and efficiency.

Develop and implement plans for the operational transition of new software and systems. Provide subject matter expertise for the development of documentation for new software and systems, including requirements and specifications, test plans and reports, and standard operating procedures.

Coordinate with other NOAA offices, government agencies, academic partners, and industry through working groups, conferences, and meetings to identify and promote collaborative work and best practices. Conduct training on new software, systems, and procedures undergoing transition to operational use.

NOTE: These duties are described at the full performance level of the ZP-4; the ZP-3 is developmental leading to such performance. This position will be filled under the DOC Alternative Personnel System (CAPS). Under CAPS, positions are classified by career, pay plan, and pay band. The ZP-3 is equivalent to the GS-11/12.

The ZP-4 is equivalent to the GS-13/14.

IT Support Specialist Information Services Division Salary: $87,271 - $90,661 This is a non-supervisory position. Job Summary: This job is with the Information Services (IS) Division, Office of the Sergeant at Arms (SAA), U.S. House of Representatives (House).

The IS division procures, manages and supports technology-related resources and projects for the Office of the SAA, and collaborates with other House offices to ensure the security and efficiency of SAA information systems.

Incumbent deploys, maintains and decommissions hardware and software (Windows computers and iOS mobile devices), provides technical support (phone, email and desk-side), and assists with technical projects. Incumbent must possess strong technical and customer service skills and be able to efficiently multi-task in a fast-paced environment.

Ability to stay organized and communicate effectively is a must.

Duties: Typical duties include, but are not necessarily limited to: Configures and deploys desktops computers, laptops, peripherals and mobile devices Creates and manages Active Directory user accounts and distribution groups Troubleshoots desktop and mobile device problems Provides technical phone and desk-side support to end users Supports disaster recovery and business continuity programs
Job Requirements: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience. Intimate working knowledge of desktop operating systems Preferred Qualifications: N/A Skill Requirements: CORE Adaptability - Ability to deal calmly and effectively with high stress situations and work persistently when facing obstacles.

Ability to work well in ambiguous situations, adjust quickly to change, and easily consider new approaches. Collaboration - Ability to foster a sense of unity and trust within teams, breaking down silos and promoting teamwork across departments. Ability to encourage and facilitate cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity.

Skill in working with others to achieve goals. Communication - Ability to convey ideas and information to different audiences through verbal and written means. Knowledge of different writing techniques for different document types and purposes. Ability to create written documents that are complete, grammatically accurate, and technically sound.

Ability to articulate ideas clearly through speech. Customer Orientation - Values and delivers high quality, professional, responsive, and innovative service to internal and external customers. Builds and maintains effective customer relations that result in satisfaction; holds self and others accountable for quality outcomes.

Decision Making - Skill in making sound, well-informed, and objective decisions, taking into consideration the potential impact and implications of the decisions. Ability to commit to action even in uncertain situations. Organizational Awareness - Knowledge of the structure, functions, and dynamics present within the U.S.

House of Representatives and the SAA. Knowledge of relevant policies and procedures that govern the organization. Knowledge of how the SAA fits within the broader context of Federal agencies and how it contributes to government functioning. Planning and Coordination - Ability to organize work, set priorities, and determine resource requirements.

Ability to determine short- or long-term goals and strategies to achieve them. Ability to coordinate with others to accomplish goals. Skill in monitoring progress in relation to desired outcomes. Problem Solving - Ability to identify problems; skill in determining accuracy and relevance of information.

Ability to use sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, develop effective solutions, and make recommendations. LEADERSHIP Leadership skills are not a requirement at entry for this job, but may be required at a later point to fulfill the duties of the job.

SPECIALTY Information Security - Knowledge of the principles, methods, and tools for protecting information and information systems from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction in order to provide confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Work Schedule: Full-time, permanent.

Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. Must be able to work outside of normal business hours - evenings and weekends may be required. Physical Requirements and Work Environment: This job is based in a typical office environment. Role requires equipment weighing up to 25 lbs.

The incumbent should be capable of meeting physical requirements, which may include sitting, lifting, bending, crouching, walking, and standing. Other Significant Factors: Job requires on-call support. Job requires local travel within the Washington, DC metropolitan area. Job may be required to report to work in all conditions.

Job may require various shifts, extended hours or weekends. Applicant Instructions: Qualified candidates should submit a resume and cover letter by 7:00 p.m. on August 3, 2026. Applicants will receive an email response indicating receipt of their cover letter and resume. Submission of these documents does not guarantee an interview.

Applicants will be considered without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, sex (including marital or parental status), disability, or age. The SAA is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to building and maintaining an inclusive and diverse work environment. Employment with the U.S. House of Representatives is at-will.

This position has been determined to be Non-Exempt from the overtime provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act. Employment is contingent upon satisfactorily completing a criminal history records check. A preemployment drug test is required for positions requiring a security clearance.

Veterans’ Preference Information: Hiring for this position is governed by the Veterans Employment Opportunities Act. Only applicants seeking veterans’ preference consideration should email saa.veoa@mail.house.gov for further information. Please note the word “Veteran” in the subject line and note the job title in the body of the email.

This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-11).

The specialized experience must include, or be supplemented by, information technology related experience (paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training, as appropriate) which demonstrates each of the four competencies, as defined: (1) Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail.

Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: completing thorough and accurate work independently, even in the most difficult or stressful situations; occasionally reviewing work completed by others.

(2) Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services.

Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: resolving routine and non-routine problems, questions, or complaints; developing and maintaining strong, mutually supportive working relationships with customers; conducting evaluation of support to determine quality of services and customer satisfaction, and recommending procedural changes based on customer need or changes in policy and/or regulation.

(3) Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately.

Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: convincingly conveying complex information to customers; presenting thoughts that are well-organized and demonstrating confidence in the facts and ideas; adjusting style when working with individuals with different levels of understanding; using various methods to explain and convey information.

(4) Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations.

Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: solving complex or sensitive problems by developing and proposing strategic alternatives; identifying possible conflicts and shared benefits; helping team anticipate problems and identifying and evaluating potential sources of information; providing feedback and coaching to others to help solve problems; engaging appropriate stakeholders when developing solutions in order to understand and incorporate multiple perspectives and needs; evaluating the effectiveness of decisions and adjusting future decisions as appropriate.

FOR GS-11 CONSIDERATION: Applicants must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-09 grade level in the Federal service or equivalent responsibility in the private sector/pay systems.

Using initiative and resourcefulness in researching IT trends and patterns to adapt or modify traditional methods.

Assisting in eliciting, documenting, analyzing, and interpreting requirements/user stories for business process automation, and ensure compliance with IT policy directives governing business application software development and standards. Working on multiple projects concurrently, at various stages of the software development lifecycle.

OR Education: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree, or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree. OR Combination of Education and Experience: You must have an appropriate combination of successfully completed graduate level education and experience. The quality of the combination of education and experience must be sufficient to demonstrate that you possesses the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform work in the occupation.

To determine your combination, first compute your experience as a percentage of the experience listed in the job announcement (1 year of specialized experience); then determine your education as a percentage of the education listed above; then add the two percentages. The total percentages must equal at least 100 percent.

Only graduate education in excess of 2 years (36 semester hours) may be used to qualify. FOR GS-12 CONSIDERATION: Applicants must have one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level in the Federal service or equivalent responsibility in the private sector/pay systems.

Assisting in eliciting, documenting, analyzing, and interpreting requirements/user stories for business process automation, within compliance with policy directives governing business application software development standards. Working on multiple projects concurrently, at various stages of the software development lifecycle.

Working knowledge of software tool(s) to track requirements/user stories. Guiding the customers through the IT governance process. Participating in peer reviews and inspection of IT documentation. Participating in prioritizing program areas' business requirements and user stories. Identifying potential information technology (IT) improvements.

Developing, documenting, and managing business requirements/user stories. Working knowledge of agile software development methodology and processes.

Leading the eliciting, documenting, analyzing, and interpreting requirements/user stories for business process automation, within compliance with policy directives governing business application software development standards. Experience with software tool(s) to track requirements/user stories.

Working on multiple projects concurrently, at various stages of the software development lifecycle. Identifying potential information technology (IT) improvements. Utilizing agile software development methodology and processes. Guiding the customers and actively participating in the IT governance process. Actively participating in peer reviews and inspection of IT documentation. Recommending process improvement to IT governance process.

Actively participating in prioritizing program areas' business requirements and user stories. Atticus is hiring an IT Specialist to own and mature our internal IT operations as we scale.

You’ll work closely with and report to the Information Security Manager, supporting day-to-day IT operations while helping improve the systems, processes, and tooling we rely on across endpoint device lifecycle management, identity and access, SaaS administration, and our broader cloud-first IT environment.

About us Atticus is a Melbourne-based scale-up founded in 2017, which offers the leading technology in document fact-checking. We are on a mission to ensure every critical document is accurate and defensible. Our software helps our customers (law firms, listed companies, and funds) fact-check critical documents before they are disclosed to market.

Our users love Atticus because we save them a lot of pain in high stakes work. We are a small, highly efficient team that relies on well-run internal systems to stay productive. As we grow, we are committed to preserving that speed while maintaining the security, reliability, and trust our customers expect.

That means giving our people simple, dependable tools and support, while ensuring our devices, access, and SaaS systems are managed in a secure and scalable way. About the role As our IT Specialist, you will keep Atticus ’s internal IT operations running smoothly while helping us build a more scalable, secure, and reliable technology environment.

You’ll act as a first point of contact with users, manage devices and access, improve integrations between platforms, and ensure our internal tools are reliable, secure, and easy to use. As a small and highly efficient company, this is a broad role suited to someone comfortable operating across multiple areas of IT.

You’ll need to take initiative, solve ambiguous or unfamiliar problems, follow through reliably, and balance responsive support with longer-term improvement work. From time to time, the role may involve after-hours support for our UK team, particularly for onboarding, offboarding, or urgent support needs.

You will also be accountable for driving the pace of projects that strengthen how we manage identity, devices, applications, data, and access. You’ll be working across a range of responsibilities that support the smooth running and ongoing improvement of our internal IT operations:

Internal IT support: Providing end-to-end technical support across user devices, applications, account access, and collaboration tools, helping staff resolve issues quickly with minimal disruption to their work.

Endpoint lifecycle management: Managing the full lifecycle of endpoint devices — primarily that our Apple fleet is consistently enrolled, configured, patched, and compliant, with a repeatable and well-documented lifecycle process from procurement through to retirement.

Apple device management & automation: Writing and maintaining scripts to support macOS administration, MDM workflows, app deployment, and compliance checks, improving consistency and scalability as we grow.

Identity & access management: Managing accounts, permissions, and access changes are managed accurately and promptly, onboarding and offboarding workflows are automated, and our IAM practices mature in line with the needs of the business.

SaaS & business systems administration: Managing and optimising core SaaS platforms to keep them reliable, secure, and well-integrated, while improving visibility and governance across the application stack.

Process improvement & automation: Identifying, prioritising, and improving manual IT processes to create faster workflows, reduce errors, and support a more scalable IT operation.

Security-aligned operations: Partnering with the Information Security Manager to ensure IT operations support broader security objectives across devices, users, applications, and access.

Documentation: Developing and maintaining technical documentation, runbooks, and user guides for end users, IT/security stakeholders, and future team members.
About you We’re looking for a capable and proactive IT professional with 3+ years of experience in IT, systems administration, endpoint management, IT operations, or a similar role. You enjoy helping people solve practical technology problems, but also care about improving the systems, processes, and automation that reduce friction over time.

You have a strong sense of ownership, are comfortable working independently in a broad role, and are looking for an opportunity to take greater ownership of a modern, cloud-first internal IT environment.

You have hands-on experience managing user devices, access, SaaS platforms, and identity-related tooling, and are comfortable balancing responsive support with longer-term improvement work.

You do not need to have worked with every tool we use, but you should be practical, curious, technically confident, and willing to learn unfamiliar systems when needed. So if you’ve got the following skills and capabilities then please get in touch:

Internal IT & user support: Experience providing end-to-end technical support across hardware, software, accounts, collaboration tools, and internal systems, including troubleshooting, escalations, and Apple device support.

Endpoint & device management: Solid understanding of endpoint management in macOS and Apple environments, including MDM, device enrolment, configuration, app deployment, patching, compliance, and the full device lifecycle.

Apple administration & scripting: Strong working knowledge of macOS administration with the ability to write or maintain scripts for Apple/Unix environments to support MDM workflows, app deployment, reporting, and repeatable IT operations.

Identity & access management: Experience managing identities, accounts, permissions, and lifecycle processes across business systems, with an understanding of identity providers, MFA, SSO, SCIM, and centralised access management.

SaaS & business systems administration: Experience managing and optimising SaaS platforms, including user access, configuration, integrations, and documentation, with an interest in reducing complexity and unmanaged technology sprawl.

Security-aligned IT operations: Familiarity with security controls relevant to IT operations — device compliance, endpoint protection, identity governance, data protection, and application visibility — without needing to be a security specialist.

Systems integration & process improvement: Experience reviewing workflows, identifying inefficiencies, and delivering practical improvements that connect systems, reduce manual effort, and make operations more scalable.

Documentation & technical communication: Able to produce clear documentation, procedures, and user guidance, adapting communication style for technical and non-technical audiences alike.

Security & compliance awareness: Familiarity with security frameworks and how organisations implement security controls, with comfort working in environments where IT supports security, auditability, and customer trust.

Qualifications & certifications: Relevant IT qualifications or equivalent experience are valued. Useful certifications include SC-300, Apple device management training, Okta Certified Administrator, Google Workspace Administrator, Jamf 100/200/300, CompTIA A+/Network+/Security+/Linux+, LFCS, or RHCSA, though none are required.

comstruct builds AI agents for construction. We're looking for exceptional talent to help us bring this to an industry that still runs most of it by hand.

As our Founding Customer Support Engineer you own what happens after go-live: you keep our customers' integrations running and their teams using comstruct every day.
When a delivery note doesn't map to the right project, a 3-way match fails, or data stops flowing from a customer's SAP, you own the problem end to end. You dig into logs, APIs, and data flows to find the root cause, prepare and ship smaller pull requests yourself, and work closely with engineering on more complex fixes. When you're not deep in a technical problem, you're on calls with customers, making sure the teams that went live keep using comstruct in their daily work.
You're the person the customer calls when something breaks and the one who makes sure it doesn't break again. Inside comstruct you're the voice of the customer: you spot the feature gaps that surface in real use and prioritize with the Product Engineering team which ones get built.
The deeper you get into how the product works and where it falls short, the more the door opens to move into a Forward Deployed Engineer or Product Engineering role and ship those fixes and features yourself.

Own inquiries end-to-end: Our customers run some of the largest construction sites in Europe. When something breaks, it's real: trucks, deliveries, invoices, deadlines.
Automate support with our own agents: We sell AI agents; support is a function where we also deploy them internally. You'll work out which parts of the flow an agent can handle and where the human touch still wins.
Ship the fix when it's yours to ship: Small PRs, config and mapping changes, data repair scripts, clearer error handling. Reviewed by engineering, shipped by you.
Kill recurring issues: Every ticket is a data point. You spot the patterns, bring them to Product Engineering with evidence, and push for the change that makes that ticket class disappear.
Build the support foundation: Playbook, macros, help center, internal runbooks. You won't inherit a finished system. You'll write the first version of it as you learn, with the founders and engineering behind you.

Notre solution est l'outil de travail principal de nos cabinets comptables, partenaires et dirigeants. La qualité du travail de ces utilisateurs dépend donc grandement de la qualité de notre solution.

Identifier les problématiques récurrentes, remonter les tendances observées et participer activement à l’amélioration continue du produit et des process internes.

Participer à la montée en compétence des membres de l’équipe, partager les bonnes pratiques et contribuer à une culture collaborative et orientée résolution.

· Tu disposes d’une bonne compréhension des outils techniques : API REST, Postman, Swagger (des connaissances SQL sont un plus)

s.t:
💻 Make ourselves known as a groundbreaking accounting and financial software for small businesses and their accountants

🎯 The missions
· Helpdesk: you will provide support for our teams in Paris and remotely (ticketing and training). There is no network administration or hardware repair.
· Onboarding/Offboarding: You are handle for equipment and software provisioning, machine preparation, and introducing new employees to our IT environment and security protocols. You will also manage the operations for external partners and freelancers.
· Security Compliance: you manage IT Security metrics monitoring (alerts), as well as non compliance against our internal IT policies (shadow hardware, security bypass, etc.)
· Software Administration : You will manage access to all our tools, including account creation and rights management, while monitoring and auditing these processes.
· Training: you will organize global and specialized trainings to ensure that our teams are as efficient as possible on our tools and that they are aware of security issues. You will also set up a knowledge base, monitoring tools, etc.

Für unser Team suchen wir eine kommunikative und lösungsorientierte Persönlichkeit für die fachliche Betreuung und den Support rund um unsere Applikation Tutoris. · Entgegennahme und Bearbeitung von Supportanfragen per E-Mail, Telefon oder Ticketsystem
· Dokumentation von Kundenfragen und Lösungswegen

· Freude am Support und an der täglichen Arbeit mit Anwender:innen hast

· bei komplexen technischen Fragestellungen lieber auf eine klare Vorgabe zurückgreifst, als selbst auf Ursachensuche zu gehen
· am liebsten innerhalb Deines Teams arbeitest - bei uns ist die Zusammenarbeit mit Entwicklung, Sales und Projektleitung tägliche Praxis

· Internationale Vernetzung: Teil der Volaris Group mit Zugang zu einem globalen Netzwerk

provide technical and analytical guidance and support for telecommunications systems while considering the telecommunications needs of users, operational practices and procedures, message handling practices and procedures, message handling techniques, local and wide area computer network requirements, communications security requirements and similar specialized knowledge of information technology; provide highly complex technical and operational solutions that support unique command and control telecommunications systems requirements; ensure the proper use, management, and training of all supervised personnel, consisting of multiple technical disciplines; practice efficient position management and ensures position descriptions of subordinates are accurate; realign duties within the flight to ensure efficient use of assigned manpower to accomplish unit's mission; consult with users and managers to determine specific locations and requirements for the particular system installation; identify requirements for and coordinate necessary improvements with customers; develop technical solutions to support equipment installation; direct, recommend, and implement remedial actions to correct problems or deficiencies; advise the Commander of significant issues and matters affecting the design, capabilities, and security of the unit's telecommunications systems; interview and recommend selection of new employees; provide training and orientation; ensure new employees are briefed in their duties and responsibilities; establish work performance standards and discuss and assign annual performance evaluations; initiate disciplinary actions, promotion actions and step increases; recommend awards and approve leave; manage overall personnel program within the section; plan, develop, and implement local policies, procedures, and goals for effective administration, direction, management, and operation of the section; maintain current information on system/equipment status, modifications, and related matters through on-site visits and use of unit support functions in order to analyze and report the organizations mission support posture; initiate action required to maintain maximum degrees of efficiency and reliability; maintain constant coordination between workgroups inside and outside of the unit, because complexity, cost, and uniqueness of the work involved require considerable planning and coordination; work to bring many resources together in a timed and coordinated sequence to accomplish projects in a timely and efficient manner; keep abreast of frequent, substantial, and unexpected changes in work operations and other external requirements that impact the timing and effective use of resources; establish and implement Customer Service Center (Help Desk) to receive trouble calls and complaints from all supported customers; maintain an automated/manual trouble log to ensure troubles or dissatisfaction of customers are corrected and resolved; oversee telephone systems administration; prepare and submit budget estimates and revisions for the procurement, installation, and operation/maintenance of equipment and supply items; monitor logistic support planning and programmed requirements for new equipment as required; analyze and evaluate new requirements and recommend most efficient completion method; ensure formulation of comprehensive training plans for each function and specialty within the section; ensure drill status guardsmen (DSG) are properly trained and able to perform the telecommunications activities; monitor and control the expenditure for material and manpower resources in accomplishment of peacetime and wartime mission goals; identify resource shortages or projected shortages to the commander; exercise continuing responsibility for safety conditions, procedures, and work practices employed within the maintenance community; provide work force guidance on safety matters and ensures safe work practices are utilized; ensure periodic inspections of work centers are performed and immediate action is taken to correct unsafe conditions; perform other duties as assigned.

You're energized by solving complex problems across enterprise cloud environments, analyzing performance data, isolating root causes, documenting solutions, and driving preventive measures to maintain service continuity.

OPM Qualifications Standards are available at Competency-Based Qualification Standard for the Information Technology Management Series, 2210.

Specialized Experience is experience that has equipped applicants with the particular knowledge, skills and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position, and that is typically in or related to the position to be filled.

To be creditable, you must possess one full year (52 weeks) of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade in the Federal service.

For this position, the next lower grade level is a GS-12 Specialized experience for this position includes: Experience engineering, implementing, and administering Microsoft M365 and/or Azure cloud environments, including configuration management, access controls, identity management, data protection and retention, and compliance with governance policies and security requirements; AND Experience monitoring, troubleshooting, and resolving complex issues in enterprise cloud environments, including analyzing usage and performance data, isolating configuration problems, and implementing solutions to meet operational and customer requirements; AND Experience collaborating with technical and business stakeholders to gather, analyze, and translate functional requirements into technical designs and customer delivery models, ensuring alignment with organizational goals, security mandates, and operational needs; AND Experience developing and maintaining technical documentation, standard operating procedures, and lifecycle management artifacts in support of enterprise cloud systems, including participation in certification, accreditation, and compliance activities.

For this position, the next lower grade level is a GS-13 Specialized experience for this position includes: Experience serving as a recognized technical authority on Microsoft M365 and/or Azure cloud environments, defining enterprise-wide configuration baselines, security architectures, and data protection strategies, and making decisions that significantly influence IT policies and programs; AND Experience isolating and resolving unprecedented, enterprise-impacting technical conditions in cloud environments, applying advanced analytical methods to identify systemic risks, and engineering remediation strategies that strengthen organizational resilience and prevent future disruptions; AND Experience driving consensus among senior management, cross-agency partners, cybersecurity teams, and vendors to develop technology roadmaps, shape enterprise cloud architecture, and influence the adoption of standards and policies across multiple organizational boundaries; AND Experience establishing enterprise-level technical standards, governance frameworks, and lifecycle management programs for cloud systems, directing accreditation and compliance activities, and serving as a subject matter authority that other technical experts rely on for guidance and direction.

Basic Requirement Competencies: The specialized experience must include, or be supplemented by, information technology related experience (paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training, as appropriate) which demonstrates each of the competencies, as defined: Attention to Detail Customer Service Decision Making Information Management Interpersonal Skills Oral Communication Problem Solving Teamwork Technical Competency Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Make a meaningful impact on Veteran safety by helping lead a Sterile Processing Service that supports high-quality care throughout the VA Black Hills Health Care System.

As Assistant Chief, you will work alongside Sterile Processing leadership and interdisciplinary partners to strengthen safe, reliable reprocessing practices, advance infection prevention, develop staff expertise, and drive improvements in quality and operations.

This leadership opportunity offers the chance to influence practices across the service, mentor staff and clinical partners, use data to identify opportunities for improvement, and help ensure reusable medical devices are consistently prepared to support safe Veteran care.

Duties include, but are not limited to: - Leads key Sterile Processing Service operations involving decontamination, sterilization, high-level disinfection, sterile storage, and the safe reprocessing of critical and semi-critical reusable medical devices. - Assists the Chief of Sterile Processing Service with oversight of the department, including program development, operational planning, resource management, and evaluation of service-level outcomes. - Directs quality management activities by assessing processes, monitoring trends, analyzing data, and developing corrective action plans to strengthen instrument processing and reprocessing practices. - Develops and implements policies, programs, systems, standard operating procedures, and evidence-based practices that promote safe, consistent, and effective sterile processing operations. - Provides leadership for the selection, operation, maintenance, and appropriate use of equipment involved in the reprocessing of reusable medical devices. - Develops educational programs, mentors staff and medical providers, and promotes knowledge of sterile processing principles, infection prevention, reprocessing standards, and safe clinical practices. - Collaborates with clinical and interdisciplinary partners to identify risks, address negative trends and environment-of-care concerns, and improve the safety and reliability of reusable medical device processes. - Advances performance improvement through project development, data collection, statistical analysis, and the development of evidence-based clinical guidelines and protocols that support quality Veteran care.
